long_biography.plain_text:
Australian businessman Ric Stowe developed Bluewaters power station to turn coal from his Collie mine into electricity. To accelerate construction, he paid staff bonuses for longer hours and arranged a Jimmy Barnes concert to thank workers. The project extended his business beyond supplying fuel into producing power.

His acquisitions also reached the access-equipment industry. Buying W. R. Carpenter brought Instant Access Australia into his group, and that company's licensing relationship with UpRight led to the purchase of the American manufacturer. He subsequently sold the Australian access business to managers and a financial investor. A separate branch of his interests retained Instant Upright after the Griffin collapse.
